note: EDITORIAL rulings on element photographs (round 3 §47.3). The chemistry stage takes each element's Wikidata P18 image through the Commons licence gate; this file overrides the automatic choice where P18 is not a photograph of the element itself. An entry with noSample:true says, with a reason, that no macroscopic sample of the element has ever been photographed (or exists); the panel then shows the discovering facility's photo (facility = Wikidata id, whose own P18 is licence-gated in the same way) or a labelled placeholder, never a substitute passed off as a sample. sampleNote annotates a genuine sample photo that needs context.

facilities.Q703993: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research, Darmstadt, Germany

85.sampleNote: The only photograph of astatine ever taken: the blue glow of about 40 nanograms of astatine-211 in solution. No visible solid sample can exist — the element's radioactivity would vaporise it.

86.reason: Radon is a colourless radioactive gas prepared only in microgram quantities; there is no photograph of the element itself. The Commons image on its Wikidata item shows radon-water apparatus, not radon.

87.reason: Francium has never been isolated in a weighable quantity: its longest-lived isotope has a 22-minute half-life, and the largest sample ever assembled was some 300,000 atoms held in a magneto-optical trap. The Commons image on its Wikidata item is a museum placard, so it is not used.

100.sampleNote: A fermium–ytterbium alloy used to measure fermium's enthalpy of vaporisation; fermium has never been isolated as a bulk metal on its own.
